report.summary: Gate 0 allows new feature paths outside contracts if labelled experimental, defeating intent; Gate 1 forbids auto-merge but no mechanism prevents it; Gate 3 baseline list may be incomplete; Gate 4 oracle graph control is undefined; Gate 5 permits 'Beats AlphaEvolve' with narrow proxy, enabling inflated claims.
risks: 10.1 | high | 'explicitly labelled experimental' allows any later-gate prototype to bypass canonical contracts by simply adding a label, defeating Gate 0's 'no new feature path outside canonical contracts' | check if any code path labelled experimental exists that creates a new state store

10.2 | medium | 'one Event Store plus content-addressed artifact store' does not specify constraints on store implementation; could be a single shared store that violates separation of concerns | verify that Event Store and artifact store are separate logical stores with distinct APIs

10.3 | medium | 'canonical Mission, Attempt, Evidence, Campaign, policy, and receipt schemas' does not define what makes a schema canonical; could be any version | examine if there is a schema registry with versioning and approval process

10.4 | medium | 'one vendor-neutral Agent Contract / Runtime Manifest' does not specify how vendor-neutrality is enforced; could reference proprietary APIs | check that the contract does not depend on any specific vendor's SDK or service

10.5 | low | 'centralized start/guard path for every effectful runtime entrypoint' does not define what constitutes an effectful entrypoint; could be bypassed by calling internal functions directly | audit all runtime entrypoints to ensure they go through the guard

10.6 | medium | 'enforceable write/egress/spend/secrets/concurrency/kill policies' does not specify how enforcement is implemented; could be a no-op if not tied to actual runtime checks | verify that each policy type has a corresponding runtime enforcement mechanism

10.7 | medium | 'real adapter fixtures for start, stream, tool events, structured output, timeout, cancellation, workspace isolation, and cost' does not define what 'real' means; could be mock implementations | inspect each fixture to confirm it exercises the actual adapter code path

10.8 | high | 'policy coverage tests for Claude, Codex, Ollama, Web/API, MCP/File Bridge, Python entrypoints, and isolated worktrees' does not specify what coverage means; could be trivial test that only checks if policy exists | require that each test actually triggers the policy and verifies enforcement

10.9 | high | 'no new feature path or state store outside the canonical contracts' is contradicted by the preamble allowing experimental prototypes; a label suffices to circumvent | ensure that any experimental prototype does not create a new state store or feature path without explicit governance approval

10.10 | medium | 'exit only when a fault-injection matrix demonstrates fail-closed protected effects and fail-open read-only inspection' does not define the fault-injection matrix or what constitutes fail-closed/fail-open | create a documented matrix of injected faults and expected outcomes

10.11 | medium | 'Prove one vertical mission: propagate Event.voltage -> bias_voltage across Python, Markdown, and CSV' does not specify what 'prove' means; could be a single successful run | define measurable criteria for success, e.g., correct output for multiple test cases

10.12 | medium | 'Ikarus produces one MissionContract; the four planes produce two typed WorkItems' does not specify the types or how they are verified | require schema validation for the produced artifacts

10.13 | medium | 'attempts run in isolation; restart/replay works' does not define isolation guarantees or what restart/replay means | test that an attempt cannot affect another and that replay produces identical results

10.14 | high | 'No auto-merge' is a rule but there is no mechanism to prevent it; a careless engineer could implement auto-merge and still formally comply if not caught | add a CI check that rejects any merge that is not manually reviewed

10.15 | medium | 'Add function/method resolution, data/schema extraction, knowledge crosslinks, revision atomicity, evidence locators, and four-plane ablations' does not specify what these terms mean | define each term with examples and acceptance criteria
10.16 | low | 'Do not scale before the full graph beats simpler representations' does not define 'beats' or 'simpler representations' | establish a benchmark and threshold for comparison

10.17 | medium | 'Freeze public tasks, evaluator versions, budgets, model/hardware reporting, seed policy, and statistical reporting' does not specify how freezing is enforced | require that these items are version-controlled and changes require approval

10.18 | medium | 'Required baselines are Random Search, Best-of-N, a single-LLM loop, simple local mutation, BM25, embeddings, code-only graph, four separate indices, evaluator-only selection, archive/MAP-Elites, and a transparent AlphaEvolve-like proxy' does not specify implementation details; could be trivial or incorrect | verify that each baseline is implemented according to published standards

10.19 | medium | 'Measure success rate, best-so-far AUC, wall time, tokens, compute, variance, diversity, regressions, and human intervention' does not specify how to measure each metric | define measurement protocols for each metric

10.20 | medium | 'Test Graph-conditioned Representation Search first: use verified Project Twin structure to select and compress context or operators, then compare against budget-equal retrieval and evaluator-only baselines' does not specify what 'verified' means | require that the Project Twin structure is validated before use

10.21 | high | 'Controls include edge rewiring, relation-label permutation, cross-plane bridges off, stale snapshots, and an oracle graph' does not define what an oracle graph is; could be cheating if it contains future information | define oracle graph as a graph constructed from the true underlying structure, not from test data

10.22 | medium | 'One hypothesis, one pre-registered protocol, complete ablations' does not specify where the protocol is registered or what constitutes complete ablations | require pre-registration in a public repository and list all ablation conditions

10.23 | medium | 'Release reproducible task definitions, evaluator code/version, receipts, cost/latency tables, ablations, failures, and a claim bounded by observed evidence' does not specify what 'reproducible' means or how to verify | require that all artifacts are archived with checksums and a reproduction script

10.24 | high | 'Beats AlphaEvolve is permitted only for directly comparable public artifact scores under budget-equal measurements; otherwise state the narrower proxy/task result' allows a narrow proxy claim that could be misleading if the proxy is not representative | require that any 'beats' claim is accompanied by a clear statement of the comparison scope and limitations
todos: Add governance process for experimental prototypes to prevent bypass of canonical contracts
Define auto-merge prevention mechanism in CI
Specify oracle graph control to avoid data leakage
Require pre-registration of hypothesis and protocol in a public repository
Add verification steps for baseline implementations

claims.claim: A later-gate experiment may be prototyped only when it does not create a competing kernel and is explicitly labelled experimental.
claims.why: The label 'experimental' is the only condition; there is no mechanism to prevent creating a competing kernel. A careless engineer could label any prototype experimental and bypass the intent of Gate 0's 'no new feature path outside canonical contracts'. The rule as written cannot detect a violation because it only requires a label.

claims.claim: Deliver one Event Store plus content-addressed artifact store.
claims.why: The claim does not specify constraints on the stores. They could be the same store, violating separation of concerns. The rule as written does not require distinct stores or define what qualifies as 'one Event Store'.

claims.claim: Deliver canonical Mission, Attempt, Evidence, Campaign, policy, and receipt schemas.
claims.why: The term 'canonical' is not defined. Any schema could be claimed canonical. There is no registry or approval process specified.

claims.claim: Deliver one vendor-neutral Agent Contract / Runtime Manifest for capabilities, mission envelopes, tools, egress, workspace, cost, and conformance receipts.
claims.why: 'Vendor-neutral' is not defined. A contract that references proprietary APIs could still be claimed vendor-neutral. The rule does not specify how to verify neutrality.

claims.claim: Deliver centralized start/guard path for every effectful runtime entrypoint.
claims.why: The claim does not define 'effectful runtime entrypoint'. An engineer could bypass the guard by calling internal functions directly. The rule as written does not require that all entrypoints are covered.

claims.claim: Deliver enforceable write/egress/spend/secrets/concurrency/kill policies.
claims.why: 'Enforceable' is ambiguous. Policies could exist but not be tied to runtime enforcement. A formal compliance could have policy definitions that are never checked. The rule does not require actual enforcement.

claims.claim: Deliver real adapter fixtures for start, stream, tool events, structured output, timeout, cancellation, workspace isolation, and cost.
claims.why: 'Real' is not defined. Fixtures could be mock implementations that do not exercise actual adapter code. The rule does not specify how to verify they are real.

claims.claim: Deliver policy coverage tests for Claude, Codex, Ollama, Web/API, MCP/File Bridge, Python entrypoints, and isolated worktrees.
claims.why: 'Coverage' is not defined. A test that simply checks if a policy file exists would satisfy the letter but not the intent. The rule does not require that tests actually enforce the policy.

claims.claim: Deliver no new feature path or state store outside the canonical contracts.
claims.why: This claim contradicts the preamble which allows experimental prototypes. An experimental prototype could create a new feature path or state store if labelled experimental. The rule as written is not absolute and can be circumvented by a label.

claims.claim: Exit only when a fault-injection matrix demonstrates fail-closed protected effects and fail-open read-only inspection.
claims.why: The fault-injection matrix is not defined. What constitutes fail-closed or fail-open is not specified. The claim is unfalsifiable without a defined matrix and pass/fail criteria.

claims.claim: Prove one vertical mission: propagate Event.voltage -> bias_voltage across Python, Markdown, and CSV.
claims.why: 'Prove' is not defined. A single successful run could be considered proof. The rule does not specify what constitutes a proof or how many test cases are needed.

claims.claim: Ikarus produces one MissionContract; the four planes produce two typed WorkItems.
claims.why: The types of WorkItems are not specified. The claim does not define what 'typed' means or how to verify the types.

claims.claim: Attempts run in isolation; restart/replay works.
claims.why: 'Isolation' is not defined. An attempt could share state with another if not prevented. Restart/replay might not be tested. The rule does not specify how to verify these properties.

claims.claim: No auto-merge.
claims.why: This is a rule but there is no mechanism to enforce it. A careless engineer could implement auto-merge and still formally comply if no one checks. The rule as written cannot detect auto-merge.

claims.claim: Add function/method resolution, data/schema extraction, knowledge crosslinks, revision atomicity, evidence locators, and four-plane ablations.
claims.why: These terms are not defined. An engineer could implement something that satisfies the name but not the intent. The rule does not specify acceptance criteria.

claims.claim: Do not scale before the full graph beats simpler representations.
claims.why: 'Beats' is not defined. What constitutes a simpler representation is not specified. The rule is unfalsifiable without metrics.

claims.claim: Freeze public tasks, evaluator versions, budgets, model/hardware reporting, seed policy, and statistical reporting.
claims.why: 'Freeze' is not defined. Changes could occur without detection. The rule does not require version control or approval process.

claims.claim: Required baselines are Random Search, Best-of-N, a single-LLM loop, simple local mutation, BM25, embeddings, code-only graph, four separate indices, evaluator-only selection, archive/MAP-Elites, and a transparent AlphaEvolve-like proxy.
claims.why: The implementations of these baselines are not specified. A baseline could be implemented incorrectly or trivially. The rule does not define what constitutes a valid implementation.

claims.claim: Measure success rate, best-so-far AUC, wall time, tokens, compute, variance, diversity, regressions, and human intervention.
claims.why: The measurement protocols are not defined. Different definitions could yield different results. The rule does not specify how to measure each metric.

claims.claim: Test Graph-conditioned Representation Search first: use verified Project Twin structure to select and compress context or operators, then compare against budget-equal retrieval and evaluator-only baselines.
claims.why: 'Verified' is not defined. The Project Twin structure could be assumed correct without validation. The rule does not specify what verification entails.

claims.claim: Controls include edge rewiring, relation-label permutation, cross-plane bridges off, stale snapshots, and an oracle graph.
claims.why: The 'oracle graph' is not defined. It could be a graph that leaks information about the test set, invalidating the experiment. The rule does not specify constraints on the oracle graph.

claims.claim: One hypothesis, one pre-registered protocol, complete ablations.
claims.why: The registration location is not specified. 'Complete ablations' is not defined. The rule does not specify what constitutes a complete set of ablations.

claims.claim: Release reproducible task definitions, evaluator code/version, receipts, cost/latency tables, ablations, failures, and a claim bounded by observed evidence.
claims.why: 'Reproducible' is not defined. The release could lack necessary details. The rule does not specify how to verify reproducibility.

claims.claim: Beats AlphaEvolve is permitted only for directly comparable public artifact scores under budget-equal measurements; otherwise state the narrower proxy/task result.
claims.why: A narrow proxy could be chosen that is not representative. The claim could be technically true but misleading. The rule does not require that the proxy is meaningful or that limitations are clearly stated.
